overview.title: Altitude, snow and open sky
overview.p1: Michlifen is the ski and viewpoint area above Ifrane, known for winter snow and wide Middle Atlas panoramas the rest of the year. It is one of the reasons Ifrane works as a mountain base, not only a garden-city stop.
overview.p2: In season, expect ski traffic and weekend crowds. Out of season, come for the air, short walks and photos. Roads can be cold and windy — layers matter.
overview.p3: A half-day from Ifrane is enough for most visitors. Combine with a lake only if you start early.

q1.question: When is ski season?
q1.answer: Typically mid-winter when snow is sufficient — check current conditions before you go.

q2.question: Need equipment?
q2.answer: Rentals may be available in season; out of season you only need walking shoes and a jacket.

q3.question: How far from Ifrane?
q3.answer: Short drive uphill — usually under 30 minutes depending on road conditions.

q4.question: Open year-round?
q4.answer: The area is reachable most of the year; ski infrastructure is seasonal.

q5.question: Family friendly?
q5.answer: Yes for views and snow play; supervise children on slopes and roads.

food.title: Eat at altitude
food.p1: Bring snacks and a hot drink. Seasonal stalls appear in winter; options are limited otherwise.
food.p2: A full meal is easier back in Ifrane.

1.title: Check the road
1.desc: Ice and fog happen in winter — local drivers know when to delay.

2.title: Windproof layer
2.desc: The plateau is exposed even on sunny days.

3.title: Start early in season
3.desc: Weekend ski days fill parking and slopes fast.
